title: Derived coefficient restriction on ringed diagram topoi
statement:
Let $J$ be a small category and $u:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ a geometric morphism between topoi presented by small sites, with inverse image $u^{-1}$ and direct image $u_*$. On $\mathscr T=\mathscr X,\mathscr Y$ let $S_T$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, let $B_T:J\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathscr T)$ be a diagram of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $a_T:\Delta S_T\to B_T$ be a ring-diagram map. Specify compatible structural maps $u^{-1}S_Y\to S_X$ and $u^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$, where compatibility means that the square with $u^{-1}a_Y$ and $a_X$ commutes at every $j$. Realize $J$-diagrams by the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. A $B_T$-module is a diagram of module sheaves with transitions linear along those of $B_T$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\rho_T$ restrict scalars along $a_T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], into $J$-diagrams of $S_T$-modules. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact termwise $\rho_T$, and K-injective total derived direct image on these ringed diagram topoi. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\rho_Y R u_{*,B}^{J}\xrightarrow{\sim}R u_{*,S}^{J}\rho_X.$$
It is defined on the derived diagram categories before evaluation. Its normalization is comparison of the two factorizations of the common ringed-topos morphism from $(\mathscr X^J,B_X)$ to $(\mathscr Y^J,\Delta S_Y)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the small diagram sites of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization

proof.text: Work directly on the specified diagram sites. For each B_X-module M, compose f_B.underlying at M with the inverse of f_S.underlying at restriction(a_X)(M), using the common direct-image equality. This gives an isomorphism of underlying set sheaves. To prove linearity, take arbitrary generalized elements a,x,y on the target site and transpose the operation a*x+y through the common geometric adjunction. The two module_linear equations agree by the structural ring square and by the unchanged underlying sheaf of restriction. Thus the candidate respects a*x+y, hence addition (a=1) and scalar multiplication (y=0). Lift it to module morphisms. Naturality follows from the two underlying identifications. The underlying-set functor reflects isomorphisms and is faithful, giving the natural module isomorphism c and uniqueness with the stated normalization.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the small diagram sites of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization

proof.text: Restriction preserves the underlying abelian sheaf. The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects them; composing restriction with it is the original forgetful functor. Hence restriction is exact. Apply the Mathlib exact-functor derived factorization to obtain r_X,r_Y and phi_X,phi_Y. These are the actual termwise localization functors.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the small diagram sites of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization

proof.text: Construct the identity-site ringed-topos morphism r_X from a_X, with module functor exactly restriction(a_X), using the existing restriction-ringed-topos construction. Regard the commutative RingCat-valued sheaves as CommRingCat-valued sheaves without changing their underlying rings. Apply the ringed-topos derived composition theorem to (r_X,f_S). It supplies a derived functor RS and its unit etaS. At a K-injective B_X-complex I, both the restriction-derived unit and the composite-derived unit are invertible. The composition-unit equation and the invertible composition comparison therefore imply that etaS at restriction(a_X)(I) is invertible. This is acyclicity for f_S; restriction need not preserve K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the small diagram sites of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization

proof.text: Choose the K-injective right derived functor RB of f_B.modules. Form etaL at M as phiY.inverse at f_B(M) followed by rY(etaB at M), and etaR as Q(c at M), etaS at restriction(a_X)(M), and RS(phiX.inverse at M). Both are units for right derived functors of the same ordinary composite f_B.modules followed by restriction(a_Y). Indeed both are invertible on K-injectives: for etaL use exactness of restriction and etaB, and for etaR use Step 3. The K-injective derivability structure therefore proves their universal properties.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the small diagram sites of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization

proof.text: Take the unique isomorphism between these two right derived functors. Its unit equation is exactly the displayed normalization for kappa, after associating compositions. The right-derived universal property proves uniqueness of kappa; faithfulness of the underlying-set functor proves uniqueness of c even when paired with this condition. Every construction takes place on the entire diagram sites and their derived categories, before evaluation.

Step 4: kappa_{f_S,r_X} composed with kappa_{r_Y,f_B}^-1 gives the stated direction, and the diagram sites are small, also for J empty. Step 5: normalization uses the naturality clause of the composition node. Edge cases checked: J empty, J=1, identity coefficient maps, non-flat Z->Z/2, zero rings.
